canonical_question: Does the preservation of grain sizes up to 1073 K imply that the grain boundaries in this W-Ta-Cr-V system have exceptionally low mobility or high pinning forces?

question_variants.question: Does the preservation of grain sizes up to 1073 K imply that the grain boundaries in this W-Ta-Cr-V system have exceptionally low mobility or high pinning forces?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper reports that changes in grain sizes were not observed up to 1073 K, indicating exceptional thermal stability. While the specific mechanism (mobility vs. pinning) is inferred to be related to the unique defect kinetics and grain boundary chemistry (segregation), the text explicitly confirms the preservation of grain size.

answers.answer: The study confirms that changes in grain sizes were not observed in the nanocrystalline film during the thermal stability tests. The grain size distribution remained bimodal (~70% nanocrystalline ≤100 nm, some ultrafine 100-500 nm) with a single-phase BCC structure, implying the boundaries have low mobility or high pinning forces under the tested conditions.
answers.measurement_outcome: Changes in grain sizes were not observed
answers.mechanism: High thermal stability of the nanocrystalline structure
evidence_spans: A detailed characterization of the morphology and phase details of the as-deposited HEA films results in a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains with size in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm) and some regions of ultrafine grain sizes (100 to 500 nm) with an underlying single-phase BCC, with a lattice constant of ~3.2 Å
APT confirmed the EDS results, showing a film composition of 38% (±0.09) W, 36% (±0.09) Ta, 15% (±0.05) Cr, and 11% (±0.05) V.
The morphology is composed of very distinct compositional striations (layering) within the grains of ~4-nm thickness, which was not observed in EDS.
